models_evaluated: downstream chest radiograph disease classification models

links.outcome: Underdiagnosis fairness gap and accuracy after synthetic pretraining as bias mitigation
links.effect: Synthetic pretraining gave a 6.5% accuracy increase (vs 2.7% for naive real+synthetic mixing) and reduced the underdiagnosis fairness gap by 19.3%, with improvements across intersectional subgroups.
links.quote: We observe this performance improvement simultaneously with the reduction of the underdiagnosis fairness gap by 19.3%, with marked improvements across intersectional subgroups of sex, age, and race/ethnicity.

links.outcome: Performance and fairness when training with demographically balanced synthetic data
links.effect: Pretraining on a demographically balanced synthetic dataset (>565,000 images) improved performance, out-of-distribution generalization, and fairness across demographic subgroups on held-out data from five institutions.
links.quote: Through extensive evaluation on over 137,000 held-out chest radiographs from five institutions, we demonstrate that synthetic pretraining consistently improves model performance, generalization to out-of-distribution settings, and fairness across demographic subgroups defined across varying fairness metrics.

unlisted_practices: Synthetic data pretraining followed by fine-tuning on real data to improve robustness and label efficiency

screen.reason: Evaluates an AI development/training pipeline technique using controllable synthetic data generation to improve fairness and diagnostic robustness across demographic subgroups, but does not test an organizational deployment guardrail or practice.
